{"filePath": "/home/electric/workspace/EmbeddingService/deployment-guide.md", "content": "# EmbeddingService Deployment Guide

## Overview
This guide covers deploying the EmbeddingService to Kubernetes using Ray Serve for GPU-accelerated inference.

## Architecture
```
Internet → NGINX Ingress (TLS) → K8s Service → Ray Head Node (Serve proxy) → Ray GPU Workers (FastAPI replicas)
```

## Prerequisites

### 1. Kubernetes Cluster
- Kubernetes 1.20+
- GPU nodes with NVIDIA drivers installed
- `nvidia.com/gpu` resource available
- Sufficient resources:
  - Head node: 2 CPU, 8Gi memory
  - Worker nodes: 4 CPU, 16Gi memory, 1 GPU per node

### 2. Tools Installed
```bash
# Kubectl
kubectl version --client

# Helm 3.0+
helm version

# Docker (for building images)
docker --version
```

### 3. Container Registry
- Docker Hub, GCR, ECR, or private registry
- Access credentials configured
- Push permissions

## Step 1: Build and Push Docker Image

### Build Image
```bash
cd /home/electric/workspace/EmbeddingService

# Build
docker build -t embedding-service:v1.0.0 .

# Test locally (optional)
docker run --gpus all -p 8000:8000 embedding-service:v1.0.0

# Test health endpoint
curl http://localhost:8000/health
```

### Tag and Push
```bash
# Example for Docker Hub
export REGISTRY="your-dockerhub-username"
docker tag embedding-service:v1.0.0 ${REGISTRY}/embedding-service:v1.0.0
docker push ${REGISTRY}/embedding-service:v1.0.0

# Example for GCR
export REGISTRY="gcr.io/your-project-id"
docker tag embedding-service:v1.0.0 ${REGISTRY}/embedding-service:v1.0.0
docker push ${REGISTRY}/embedding-service:v1.0.0

# Example for ECR
export REGISTRY="123456789.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com"
aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin ${REGISTRY}
docker tag embedding-service:v1.0.0 ${REGISTRY}/embedding-service:v1.0.0
docker push ${REGISTRY}/embedding-service:v1.0.0
```

### Update Helm Values
```bash
# Edit helm/embedding-service/values.yaml
# Update image.repository to your registry
vim helm/embedding-service/values.yaml
```

## Step 2: Install Ray Operator

The Ray Operator manages RayCluster custom resources.

```bash
# Add KubeRay Helm repository
helm repo add kuberay https://ray-project.github.io/kuberay-helm/
helm repo update

# Install Ray Operator
helm install kuberay-operator kuberay/kuberay-operator \
  --namespace ray-system \
  --create-namespace \
  --version 1.0.0

# Verify installation
kubectl get pods -n ray-system
kubectl get crd rayclusters.ray.io
```

## Step 3: Install NGINX Ingress Controller

```bash
# Add NGINX Ingress Helm repository
helm repo add ingress-nginx https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx
helm repo update

# Install NGINX Ingress Controller
helm install ingress-nginx ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx \
  --namespace ingress-nginx \
  --create-namespace \
  --set controller.service.type=LoadBalancer

# Wait for external IP
kubectl get svc -n ingress-nginx -w

# Get external IP
export EXTERNAL_IP=$(kubectl get svc ingress-nginx-controller -n ingress-nginx -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}')
echo "Ingress External IP: ${EXTERNAL_IP}"
```

## Step 4: Install cert-manager

```bash
# Install cert-manager
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.13.0/cert-manager.yaml

# Wait for cert-manager to be ready
kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=300s deployment/cert-manager -n cert-manager
kubectl wait --for=condition=available --timeout=300s deployment/cert-manager-webhook -n cert-manager

# Create ClusterIssuer for Let's Encrypt Staging (for testing)
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata:
  name: letsencrypt-staging
spec:
  acme:
    server: https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    email: your-email@example.com  # CHANGE THIS
    privateKeySecretRef:
      name: letsencrypt-staging
    solvers:
    - http01:
        ingress:
          class: nginx
EOF

# Create ClusterIssuer for Let's Encrypt Production
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata:
  name: letsencrypt-prod
spec:
  acme:
    server: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    email: your-email@example.com  # CHANGE THIS
    privateKeySecretRef:
      name: letsencrypt-prod
    solvers:
    - http01:
        ingress:
          class: nginx
EOF

# Verify ClusterIssuers
kubectl get clusterissuer
```

## Step 5: Configure DNS

Point your domain to the Ingress external IP.

```bash
# Get external IP
kubectl get svc ingress-nginx-controller -n ingress-nginx

# Create DNS A record:
# Name: embedding.yourdomain.com (or your chosen hostname)
# Type: A
# Value: <EXTERNAL_IP from above>
# TTL: 300-3600

# Test DNS resolution (wait for propagation, ~5-60 minutes)
nslookup embedding.yourdomain.com
dig embedding.yourdomain.com
```

## Step 6: Deploy EmbeddingService

### Development Deployment
```bash
cd /home/electric/workspace/EmbeddingService

# Install with default values
helm install embedding-service ./helm/embedding-service \
  --namespace embedding-dev \
  --create-namespace

# Monitor deployment
kubectl get pods -n embedding-dev -w

# Check logs
kubectl logs -l ray.io/node-type=head -n embedding-dev -f
kubectl logs -l ray.io/node-type=worker -n embedding-dev
```

### Production Deployment
```bash
# Update values-prod.yaml with your domain and registry
vim helm/embedding-service/values-prod.yaml

# Install with production values
helm install embedding-service ./helm/embedding-service \
  -f helm/embedding-service/values-prod.yaml \
  --namespace embedding-prod \
  --create-namespace

# Monitor deployment
kubectl get pods -n embedding-prod -w
```

## Step 7: Verify Deployment

### Check Ray Cluster Status
```bash
# Get all resources
kubectl get all -n embedding-prod

# Check RayCluster
kubectl get raycluster -n embedding-prod
kubectl describe raycluster embedding-service -n embedding-prod

# Check pods
kubectl get pods -n embedding-prod
kubectl describe pod -l ray.io/cluster=embedding-service -n embedding-prod
```

### Access Ray Dashboard
```bash
# Port forward to Ray Dashboard
kubectl port-forward svc/embedding-service 8265:8265 -n embedding-prod

# Open browser to http://localhost:8265
# Check:
# - Cluster status
# - Ray Serve deployments
# - GPU utilization
```

### Test Service Endpoints

#### Test Health Endpoint
```bash
# If ingress is ready
curl https://embedding.yourdomain.com/health

# Or port-forward
kubectl port-forward svc/embedding-service 8000:8000 -n embedding-prod
curl http://localhost:8000/health
```

#### Test Embedding Endpoint
```bash
# Small request
curl -X POST https://embedding.yourdomain.com/embeddings \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "texts": ["Hello world", "Test embedding"],
    "segmentation": false
  }' | jq .

# Batch request
curl -X POST https://embedding.yourdomain.com/embeddings \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "texts": ["Text 1", "Text 2", "Text 3", "Text 4", "Text 5"],
    "segmentation": false,
    "batch_size": 32
  }' | jq .
```

## Step 8: Monitoring

### Check Metrics
```bash
# Prometheus metrics
curl https://embedding.yourdomain.com/metrics

# Or port-forward
kubectl port-forward svc/embedding-service 8000:8000 -n embedding-prod
curl http://localhost:8000/metrics
```

### GPU Utilization
```bash
# SSH into worker pod
kubectl exec -it <worker-pod-name> -n embedding-prod -- bash

# Check GPU
nvidia-smi

# Watch GPU continuously
watch -n 1 nvidia-smi
```

### Logs
```bash
# Head node logs
kubectl logs -l ray.io/node-type=head -n embedding-prod -f

# Worker logs
kubectl logs -l ray.io/node-type=worker -n embedding-prod -f

# Ray Serve logs (on head node)
kubectl logs -l ray.io/node-type=head -n embedding-prod -c deploy-ray-serve

# All logs
kubectl logs -l ray.io/cluster=embedding-service -n embedding-prod --all-containers=true -f
```

## Step 9: Load Testing

```bash
# Run load test (if you have test_large_batch.py)
python tests/test_large_batch.py --url https://embedding.yourdomain.com

# Monitor Ray Serve autoscaling
# Open Ray Dashboard: http://localhost:8265
# Go to Serve tab
# Watch replica count change based on load
```

## Scaling

### Manual Scaling

#### Scale GPU Workers
```bash
# Edit values
helm upgrade embedding-service ./helm/embedding-service \
  -f helm/embedding-service/values-prod.yaml \
  --set workers.replicas=8 \
  --namespace embedding-prod
```

#### Scale Ray Serve Replicas
```bash
# Edit values
helm upgrade embedding-service ./helm/embedding-service \
  -f helm/embedding-service/values-prod.yaml \
  --set rayServe.numReplicas=8 \
  --namespace embedding-prod
```

### Autoscaling
Ray Serve autoscaling is configured via:
- `rayServe.minReplicas`: Minimum replicas (default: 2)
- `rayServe.maxReplicas`: Maximum replicas (default: 8)
- `rayServe.targetRequestsPerReplica`: Target requests per replica (default: 10)

## Troubleshooting

### Pods Not Starting
```bash
# Check events
kubectl get events -n embedding-prod --sort-by='.lastTimestamp'

# Describe pod
kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n embedding-prod

# Common issues:
# - Image pull errors: Check registry credentials
# - GPU not available: Check node labels and GPU resources
# - Insufficient resources: Check cluster capacity
```

### Ray Cluster Not Forming
```bash
# Check head node
kubectl logs -l ray.io/node-type=head -n embedding-prod

# Check GCS (Global Control Store)
kubectl logs -l ray.io/node-type=head -n embedding-prod | grep GCS

# Verify network connectivity between pods
kubectl exec <worker-pod> -n embedding-prod -- ping <head-pod-ip>
```

### Ray Serve Not Starting
```bash
# Check init container logs
kubectl logs -l ray.io/node-type=head -n embedding-prod -c deploy-ray-serve

# Check if deployment script ran
kubectl exec -l ray.io/node-type=head -n embedding-prod -- ray status

# Manually deploy (if init container failed)
kubectl exec -l ray.io/node-type=head -n embedding-prod -- \
  python /app/src/ray_serve_deployment.py
```

### Ingress Issues
```bash
# Check Ingress
kubectl describe ingress embedding-service -n embedding-prod

# Check certificate
kubectl describe certificate embedding-service-tls -n embedding-prod

# Check certificate request
kubectl get certificaterequest -n embedding-prod

# Test without TLS first
curl -k http://<EXTERNAL_IP> -H "Host: embedding.yourdomain.com"
```

### GPU Not Utilized
```bash
# Check GPU allocation
kubectl describe pod <worker-pod> -n embedding-prod | grep nvidia.com/gpu

# Check CUDA visibility
kubectl exec <worker-pod> -n embedding-prod -- env | grep CUDA

# Check model device
kubectl exec <worker-pod> -n embedding-prod -- \
  python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.cuda.device_count())"
```

## Updating the Deployment

### Update Configuration Only
```bash
# Edit values.yaml or values-prod.yaml
vim helm/embedding-service/values-prod.yaml

# Apply changes
helm upgrade embedding-service ./helm/embedding-service \
  -f helm/embedding-service/values-prod.yaml \
  --namespace embedding-prod
```

### Update Application Code
```bash
# 1. Build new image
docker build -t embedding-service:v1.1.0 .

# 2. Push to registry
docker tag embedding-service:v1.1.0 ${REGISTRY}/embedding-service:v1.1.0
docker push ${REGISTRY}/embedding-service:v1.1.0

# 3. Update Helm values
# Edit values.yaml: image.tag = "v1.1.0"

# 4. Upgrade deployment
helm upgrade embedding-service ./helm/embedding-service \
  -f helm/embedding-service/values-prod.yaml \
  --namespace embedding-prod

# 5. Monitor rollout
kubectl rollout status raycluster/embedding-service -n embedding-prod
```

### Update Embedding Model
```bash
# Option 1: Rebuild image with new model
# Edit Dockerfile, change model name
# Follow "Update Application Code" steps above

# Option 2: Use persistent volume
# Download model to PVC
kubectl exec <head-pod> -n embedding-prod -- \
  python -c "from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer; \
  model_name='your-new-model'; \
  AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir='/mnt/ray-storage/models'); \
  AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir='/mnt/ray-storage/models')"

# Update config
helm upgrade embedding-service ./helm/embedding-service \
  -f helm/embedding-service/values-prod.yaml \
  --set embedding.defaultModel=your-new-model \
  --namespace embedding-prod
```

## Uninstalling

```bash
# Uninstall Helm release
helm uninstall embedding-service --namespace embedding-prod

# Delete namespace (optional)
kubectl delete namespace embedding-prod

# Clean up PVC (if not automatically deleted)
kubectl delete pvc -n embedding-prod --all
```

## Production Checklist

- [ ] Docker image built and pushed to registry
- [ ] Ray Operator installed
- [ ] NGINX Ingress Controller installed with external IP
- [ ] cert-manager installed with ClusterIssuers
- [ ] DNS A record created and propagated
- [ ] Helm values updated (registry, domain, email)
- [ ] EmbeddingService deployed
- [ ] All pods running and healthy
- [ ] Ray Dashboard accessible
- [ ] Health endpoint responding
- [ ] Embedding endpoint tested
- [ ] TLS certificate issued and valid
- [ ] Metrics endpoint working
- [ ] GPU utilization confirmed
- [ ] Load testing completed
- [ ] Monitoring and alerting configured
- [ ] Backup and disaster recovery plan
- [ ] Documentation updated with actual values

## Support

For issues and questions:
- Check Ray documentation: https://docs.ray.io/
- Ray Serve docs: https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/serve/
- KubeRay docs: https://ray-project.github.io/kuberay/
"}

{"filePath": "/home/electric/workspace/EmbeddingService/Dockerfile.base", "content": "# Minimal Ray base image for embedding service
# This creates a smaller, more secure base than the official Ray GPU image

FROM nvidia/cuda:12.1.0-base-ubuntu22.04

LABEL maintainer="EmbeddingService Team"
LABEL description="Minimal Ray base with CUDA support"

# Set environment variables
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PATH="/opt/conda/bin:$PATH"

# Install system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    wget \
    git \
    build-essential \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install Miniconda (lightweight Python distribution)
RUN wget --quiet https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh -O ~/miniconda.sh && \
    /bin/bash ~/miniconda.sh -b -p /opt/conda && \
    rm ~/miniconda.sh && \
    /opt/conda/bin/conda clean -afy

# Install Python 3.11 and pip
RUN conda install -y python=3.11 pip && \
    conda clean -afy

# Install Ray with minimal dependencies
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir \
    ray[default]==2.49.2 \
    && pip cache purge

# Create ray user
RUN useradd -m -u 1000 -s /bin/bash ray && \
    mkdir -p /home/ray && \
    chown -R ray:ray /home/ray

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /home/ray

# Switch to ray user
USER ray

# Verify installations
RUN python --version && \
    ray --version && \
    python -c "import ray; print(f'Ray version: {ray.__version__}')"

# Default command
CMD ["/bin/bash"]
"}

message.text: Isn't there a way to do a mutlstgae build then where those dependecies are automaticialy detected by pip

response.value: Excellent idea! Yes, we can use a multi-stage build where pip automatically detects which packages are already installed. Let me rewrite the Dockerfile to use a cleaner approach:

edits.text:
# Dockerfile for EmbeddingService on Ray Cluster
# Multi-stage build using minimal Ray base image
# Base: Custom ray-minimal:v1.0.0 (CUDA 12.1.0 runtime + Ray 2.49.2)

FROM ray-minimal:v1.0.0

LABEL maintainer="EmbeddingService Team"
LABEL description="GPU-accelerated embedding service deployed on Ray cluster"
LABEL version="1.0.0"

# Switch to root for installation
USER root

# Install additional system dependencies if needed
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    curl \
    git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Switch to ray user for installation
USER ray

# Copy requirements file
COPY --chown=ray:users requirements.txt .

# Install from requirements.txt
# pip will automatically skip packages that are already installed with the same version
# Use --no-deps for packages we know are in base, then install their missing deps
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

response.value: Actually, pip will skip already-satisfied packages by default when using `-r requirements.txt`. But the issue is that it still downloads them to check. Let me use a better approach with `pip install --upgrade --upgrade-strategy only-if-needed`:

edits.text:
# Copy requirements file
COPY --chown=ray:users requirements.txt .

# Install from requirements.txt with optimized strategy
# --upgrade-strategy only-if-needed: Only upgrade if necessary
# pip checks installed packages and skips already-satisfied requirements
# This avoids reinstalling Ray and common dependencies from base image
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade --upgrade-strategy only-if-needed -r requirements.txt

response.value: Now let's rebuild with this cleaner approach:

# Dockerfile for EmbeddingService on Ray Cluster
# Multi-stage build to minimize final image size

# ============================================
# Stage 1: Builder - Install all dependencies
# ============================================
FROM ray-minimal:v1.0.0 AS builder

USER root

# Install build dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /build

# Copy requirements
COPY requirements.txt .

# Install all Python dependencies into a virtual environment
# This allows us to copy the entire venv to the final stage
RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

# Install only packages not in base ray-minimal image
# pip will automatically skip already-satisfied packages
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# ============================================
# Stage 2: Final runtime image
# ============================================
FROM ray-minimal:v1.0.0

LABEL maintainer="EmbeddingService Team"
LABEL description="GPU-accelerated embedding service deployed on Ray cluster"
LABEL version="1.0.0"

USER root

# Install minimal runtime dependencies only
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Copy Python virtual environment from builder
COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv

# Set PATH to use the virtual environment
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Switch to ray user
USER ray

<analysis>
[Chronological Review: Walk through conversation phases: initial request → exploration → implementation → debugging → current state]

The conversation went through these phases:

1. **Initial Context**: User returned to continue work, believing the Docker image was already built and ready to update Helm chart and setup DNS for ingress.

2. **Dependency Discovery**: Discovered that `ray[serve]` was missing from requirements.in. Added it and recompiled requirements.txt, which added Ray 2.49.2 and all its dependencies.

3. **Version Alignment**: Updated Dockerfile and Helm chart from Ray 2.39.0 to Ray 2.49.2.

4. **First Build Attempts**: Multiple Docker build attempts that were interrupted by status checks or failed due to disk space issues (98% full, "No space left on device").

5. **Disk Cleanup**: Performed docker system prune operations, freeing up ~19GB total space. This accidentally removed the Ray base image.

6. **Strategy Pivot - Minimal Base Image**: User raised security/size concerns about the 11.7GB official Ray GPU image. Decided to create a minimal custom base image with just CUDA runtime + Python + Ray.

7. **Base Image Creation - First Attempt (Conda)**: Created Dockerfile.base using Miniconda, but build failed due to Conda TOS acceptance requirement in non-interactive mode.

8. **Base Image Creation - System Python**: User correctly noted Conda was overkill. Rewrote Dockerfile.base to use system Python 3.11 from Ubuntu repos. Successfully built ray-minimal:v1.0.0 (2.7GB with CUDA runtime, verified GPU access with nvidia-smi).

9. **GPU Requirements Clarification**: User pointed out the need for CUDA runtime (not just base) for nvidia-smi access. Updated base image from `nvidia/cuda:12.1.0-base-ubuntu22.04` to `nvidia/cuda:12.1.0-runtime-ubuntu22.04`.

10. **Embedding Service Dockerfile - Dependency Redundancy Issue**: Started building embedding-service Dockerfile but user noticed it was downloading Ray and all dependencies again despite them being in the base image. Attempted filtered requirements approach.

11. **Multi-Stage Build Request**: User emphatically requested a proper MULTI-STAGE build where pip automatically detects already-installed packages. Created true multi-stage Dockerfile with builder stage creating a venv.

12. **Venv Issue**: Build failed because python3.11-venv package wasn't installed in base image. Updated Dockerfile.base to include it, rebuilt base image successfully.

13. **Build Tool Optimization**: Removed build-essential from builder stage since we're using precompiled wheels. Performed another disk cleanup freeing 19GB (including removing the 11.7GB official Ray image).

14. **Current State**: Multi-stage build is actively running, currently downloading nvidia-cublas-cu12 (594.3 MB) in the builder stage (Step 7/32).

[Intent Mapping: List each explicit user request with message context]

- "okay the image is build we need to update the helm chart now with the image and setup the dns for the ingress" - Believed build was complete, wanted to proceed to deployment
- "REquirement.in requires ray[serve] and it need to be recompile. The ray dependencies aren't met" - Identified missing dependency
- "You keep interupting the process with the check though" - Complained about build interruptions
- "That base image is massive though. All it is in linux, python and ray, we don't need all the other stuff in the image" - Size/security concern about 11.7GB official image
- "Let's do a multistage build, that uses a linux bsae ubunut with python slim and install ray. Lets do this as a separate image first and the exec it and test it. Once that works we can build a multi-stage build. This is also from a security perspective" - Requested minimal base image strategy
- "we don't need anaconda becaue we are not building out an extesnive ML image. We just have a few dependecies." - Rejected Conda, requested simpler Python installation
- "We are using GPUs so the container wil have to interact with the host so we should be able to nvidia-smi" - Pointed out need for CUDA runtime
- "The ingress is nginx though so would we need to expose 443 and 80, we may want to download models as well and the ingress is http/https" - Asked about port exposure for NGINX ingress
- "build the docker image" - Direct command to start build
- "why download the image twce though the base image has these" - Questioned redundant downloads
- "compare and constrast requirements.txt and requirement-docker.txt, do you see the necessary requirements present in the former? If so, why create a new requirements?" - Questioned need for separate requirements file
- "Isn't there a way to do a mutlstgae build then where those dependecies are automaticialy detected by pip" - Asked about automatic detection
- "Create a new docker that is a MULTISTAGE build..." (repeated 15 times for emphasis) - Emphatically demanded proper multi-stage build

[Technical Inventory: Catalog all technologies, patterns, and decisions mentioned]

- **Frameworks**: FastAPI, Ray 2.49.2, Ray Serve, Uvicorn, PyTorch, Transformers
- **Container/Orchestration**: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm 3.0+, RayCluster CRD
- **Infrastructure**: NGINX Ingress Controller, cert-manager (Let's Encrypt TLS)
- **GPU Management**: CUDA 12.1.0 runtime, nvidia/cuda base images, nvidia.com/gpu resource allocation
- **Models**: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
- **Python**: 3.11 from Ubuntu 22.04 apt repositories (python3.11, python3.11-dev, python3.11-venv, python3-pip)
- **Base Images**:
  - Rejected: rayproject/ray:2.49.2-py311-gpu (11.7GB - too large, security concerns)
  - Created: ray-minimal:v1.0.0 (2.7GB with CUDA runtime + Ray + serve)
- **Docker Strategy**: Multi-stage build with virtual environment isolation
  - Stage 1 (Builder): Install all dependencies into /opt/venv
  - Stage 2 (Runtime): Copy only the venv, minimal runtime dependencies
- **Package Management**: pip only (rejected Miniconda due to TOS and complexity)
- **Disk Management**: Freed 19GB+ across multiple cleanup operations

[Code Archaeology: Document every file, function, and code change discussed]

**Files Modified/Created:**

1. **requirements.in** (modified by user):
   - Added: `ray[serve]` at the end
   - Purpose: Ensure Ray Serve dependencies are included

2. **requirements.txt** (recompiled with pip-compile):
   - Now includes: ray[serve]==2.49.2 with all 406 lines of dependencies
   - Key packages: ray, fastapi, uvicorn, transformers, torch, pyconfs, pydantic, aiohttp, etc.

3. **requirements-docker.txt** (created then abandoned):
   - Initial purpose: Avoid reinstalling packages in base image
   - Status: No longer used after switching to multi-stage build approach

4. **Dockerfile.base** (created - final version):
   ```dockerfile
   FROM nvidia/cuda:12.1.0-runtime-ubuntu22.04
   
   # Install Python and system dependencies
   RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
       python3.11 \
       python3.11-dev \
       python3.11-venv \
       python3-pip \
       ca-certificates \
       curl \
       && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
   
   # Set python3.11 as default
   RUN update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python python /usr/bin/python3.11 1 && \
       update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python3 python3 /usr/bin/python3.11 1
   
   # Upgrade pip
   RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
   
   # Install Ray with serve support
   RUN pip install --no-cache-dir ray[serve]==2.49.2 && pip cache purge
   
   # Create ray user
   RUN useradd -m -u 1000 -s /bin/bash ray && \
       mkdir -p /home/ray && \
       chown -R ray:ray /home/ray
   
   WORKDIR /home/ray
   USER ray
   
   # Verify installations
   RUN python --version && \
       ray --version && \
       python -c "import ray; print(f'Ray version: {ray.__version__}')"
   
   CMD ["/bin/bash"]
   ```
   - Built successfully as ray-minimal:v1.0.0
   - Size: 2.7GB (vs 11.7GB official image - 76% reduction)
   - Verified: Python 3.11, Ray 2.49.2, nvidia-smi working with --gpus all flag

5. **Dockerfile** (multi-stage version - final):
   ```dockerfile
   # Stage 1: Builder
   FROM ray-minimal:v1.0.0 AS builder
   
   USER root
   WORKDIR /build
   COPY requirements.txt .
   
   # Create virtual environment
   RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
   ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"
   
   # Install all dependencies (pip skips already-satisfied from base)
   RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
   
   # Stage 2: Final runtime image
   FROM ray-minimal:v1.0.0
   
   USER root
   
   # Install minimal runtime dependencies only
   RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
       curl \
       && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
   
   # Copy venv from builder
   COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv
   ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"
   
   WORKDIR /app
   USER ray
   
   # Pre-download embedding model
   ENV TRANSFORMERS_CACHE=/app/models
   ENV HF_HOME=/app/models
   RUN mkdir -p /app/models && \
       python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel; \
       model='sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'; \
       AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model, cache_dir='/app/models'); \
       AutoModel.from_pretrained(model, cache_dir='/app/models')"
   
   # Copy application code
   COPY --chown=ray:users setup.py version ./
   COPY --chown=ray:users src/ ./src/
   RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -e .
   
   RUN mkdir -p /app/logs
   
   # Expose ports: 80, 443 (NGINX ingress), 8000 (Ray Serve), 6379 (GCS), 8265 (dashboard), 10001 (client)
   EXPOSE 80 443 8000 6379 8265 10001
   
   ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
   ENV LOG_LEVEL=INFO
   ENV SERVICE_PORT=8000
   ENV TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=0
   ENV HF_HUB_OFFLINE=0
   
   HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=60s --retries=3 \
     CMD ray health-check 2>&1 || exit 1
   
   CMD ["ray", "start", "--block"]
   ```

{"filePath": "/home/electric/workspace/EmbeddingService/Dockerfile.multistage", "content": "# Multi-stage Dockerfile for EmbeddingService
# Stage 1: Minimal Ray base with CUDA
# Stage 2: Add application dependencies and code

# ============================================
# Stage 1: Build minimal Ray base
# ============================================
FROM nvidia/cuda:12.1.0-runtime-ubuntu22.04 AS ray-base

LABEL maintainer="EmbeddingService Team"

# Set environment variables
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1

# Install Python and system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    python3.11 \
    python3.11-dev \
    python3.11-venv \
    python3-pip \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Update alternatives to use python3.11 as default
RUN update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python python /usr/bin/python3.11 1 && \
    update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python3 python3 /usr/bin/python3.11 1

# Upgrade pip
RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip setuptools wheel

# Install Ray with serve support
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir ray[serve]==2.49.2 && pip cache purge

# Create ray user
RUN useradd -m -u 1000 -s /bin/bash ray && \
    mkdir -p /home/ray && \
    chown -R ray:ray /home/ray

# Verify Ray installation
RUN python -c "import ray; from ray import serve; print(f'Ray {ray.__version__} with Serve')"

# ============================================
# Stage 2: Add application dependencies
# ============================================
FROM ray-base AS app-builder

USER root
WORKDIR /build

# Copy requirements
COPY requirements.txt .

# Create virtual environment and install dependencies
RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

# Install all Python dependencies
# Ray is already in the system, but we install into venv for isolation
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# ============================================
# Stage 3: Final runtime image
# ============================================
FROM ray-base

LABEL description="GPU-accelerated embedding service on Ray cluster"
LABEL version="1.0.0"

USER root

# Install minimal runtime dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Copy virtual environment from builder
COPY --from=app-builder /opt/venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Switch to ray user
USER ray

# Pre-download the default embedding model
ENV TRANSFORMERS_CACHE=/app/models
ENV HF_HOME=/app/models
RUN mkdir -p /app/models && \
    python -c "\
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel; \
model_name = 'sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2'; \
print(f'Downloading model: {model_name}'); \
AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir='/app/models'); \
AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, cache_dir='/app/models'); \
print('Model download complete')"

# Copy application code
COPY --chown=ray:users setup.py version ./
COPY --chown=ray:users src/ ./src/

# Install package in editable mode
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -e .

# Create logs directory
RUN mkdir -p /app/logs

# Expose ports
# 80: HTTP (for NGINX ingress)
# 443: HTTPS (for NGINX ingress with TLS)
# 8000: Ray Serve HTTP endpoint (primary service port)
# 6379: Ray GCS (Global Control Service)
# 8265: Ray Dashboard
# 10001: Ray Client
EXPOSE 80 443 8000 6379 8265 10001

# Environment variables (can be overridden by K8s)
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    LOG_LEVEL=INFO \
    SERVICE_PORT=8000 \
    TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=0 \
    HF_HUB_OFFLINE=0

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=60s --retries=3 \
  CMD ray health-check 2>&1 || exit 1

# Default command: Start Ray worker
CMD ["ray", "start", "--block"]
"}

# Todo List

- [x] Update Python config to read from environment
  - Modify src/config.py to read configuration values from environment variables (populated by K8s ConfigMap) with sensible defaults. Ensure embedding, service, and logging configs are env-aware.
- [x] Create Ray Serve deployment script
  - Write src/ray_serve_deployment.py that wraps the FastAPI app as a Ray Serve deployment. Read num_replicas, autoscaling config, and ray_actor_options from environment variables (not hardcoded).
- [x] Write Dockerfile for Ray cluster image
  - Create Dockerfile based on rayproject/ray:2.39.0-py311-gpu. Install dependencies, pre-download model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), copy src/ code, set entrypoint for Ray workers.
- [-] Build and push Docker image
  - Build Docker image locally, test model loading and Ray compatibility, tag with version (v1.0.0), and push to container registry.
- [x] Create Helm chart structure
  - Initialize Helm chart directory (helm create embedding-service), create values.yaml with all config (cluster, image, service, embedding, rayServe, workers, ingress). Ensure single source of truth.
- [x] Write Helm templates
  - Create templates/: raycluster.yaml (RayCluster CR), configmap.yaml (env vars from values), service.yaml (ClusterIP to head node), ingress.yaml (TLS + cert-manager), _helpers.tpl (labels/selectors).
- [ ] Set up NGINX Ingress Controller
  - Install ingress-nginx on K8s cluster if not present. Verify external IP assignment and that LoadBalancer is reachable.
- [ ] Set up cert-manager for TLS
  - Install cert-manager, create ClusterIssuer for Let's Encrypt (staging and prod), test certificate issuance with a simple Ingress.
- [ ] Deploy Ray cluster to K8s
  - helm install embedding-service ./helm/embedding-service -f values.yaml. Monitor pod startup, verify head and worker pods running, check Ray dashboard accessibility.
- [ ] Deploy Ray Serve to cluster
  - Run Ray Serve deployment script on head node (via init container or kubectl exec). Verify replicas start on GPU workers, check Ray dashboard shows deployments.
- [ ] Create K8s Service and Ingress
  - Apply Service (pointing to head node port 8000) and Ingress manifests. Verify cert-manager creates TLS certificate. Test internal cluster access first.
- [ ] Configure DNS
  - Get Ingress external IP, create DNS A record (embedding.yourdomain.com → external IP), wait for DNS propagation, test with nslookup/dig.
- [ ] Validation and smoke testing
  - Test /health and /health/ready endpoints via Ingress. Run small embedding requests, verify responses. Check GPU utilization in worker pods (nvidia-smi). Inspect logs for errors.
- [ ] Load testing and tuning
  - Run test_large_batch.py against production URL. Monitor Ray dashboard for autoscaling events. Tune rayServe.targetRequestsPerReplica and worker resources based on performance.
- [ ] Set up monitoring and observability
  - Configure Prometheus to scrape /metrics endpoint. Create Grafana dashboards for request rate, latency, GPU utilization, Ray replica status. Set up alerting for pod failures and high error rates.
- [ ] Document deployment and operations
  - Write deployment guide (README or runbook) covering: how to deploy, how to scale, how to update config, how to troubleshoot common issues, how to update the model.
